title: Selective photocatalytic oxidation of cyclohexane to KA-oil over carbon-supported TiO 2  nanoparticles
content: Carbon-supported TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized and evaluated as photocatalysts for the selective oxidation of cyclohexane under UV irradiation. In the presence of H2O2 as a green oxidant and under mild reaction conditions, the catalysts achieved a cyclohexane conversion of 30.2% with 85% selectivity toward KA-oil, consisting of cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone. The hybrid photocatalyst exhibited excellent recyclability, maintaining its activity and selectivity over five consecutive cycles with negligible performance loss. The enhanced catalytic efficiency was attributed to improved charge separation promoted by the carbon support and the effective generation of reactive oxygen species. Comprehensive characterization, including XRD, TEM, BET, DRS, and FTIR, revealed strong correlations between the catalysts' structural and optical properties and their catalytic performance. Scavenging experiments using tert-butanol (t-BuOH) and disodium ethylenediaminetetraacetate (EDTA-2Na) further supported the involvement of reactive oxygen species in the reaction mechanism.
